lines.text: Here's a fence with one bend, tucked into a corner. How much ground can it hold?
lines.caption: Here's a fence with one bend, tucked into a corner. How much ground can it hold?

lines.text: Most kids bend it into a square. <short pause> But a square is NOT the best you can do!
lines.caption: Most kids bend it into a square. But a square is NOT the best you can do!

lines.text: Hi, I'm Vantee! Let's find the best shape with a mirror trick.
lines.caption: Hi, I'm Vantee! Let's find the best shape with a mirror trick.

lines.text: Here's the question. Two straight walls meet at a right angle.
lines.caption: Here's the question. Two straight walls meet at a right angle.

lines.text: A fence made of two straight pieces runs from one wall to the other, bending once.
lines.caption: A fence made of two straight pieces runs from one wall to the other, bending once.

lines.text: The two pieces have a total length of twelve. The fence and the walls enclose a region.
lines.caption: The two pieces have a total length of twelve. The fence and the walls enclose a region.

lines.text: What is the largest possible area of the region? Here are the five choices.
lines.caption: What is the largest possible area of the region? Here are the five choices.

lines.text: Let's name things. Call the corner O, the fence ends A and B, and the bend P.
lines.caption: Let's name things. Call the corner O, the fence ends A and B, and the bend P.

lines.text: The walls are free. We choose where the ends go, how long each piece is, and the bend.
lines.caption: The walls are free. We choose where the ends go, how long each piece is, and the bend.

lines.text: Bend it into a six by six square, and the area is thirty-six.
lines.caption: Bend it into a six by six square, and the area is thirty-six.

lines.text: A straight fence across, with equal legs of six root two, also gives thirty-six. Can a bend do better?
lines.caption: A straight fence across, with equal legs of six root two, also gives thirty-six. Can a bend do better?

lines.text: Now it's your turn. Pause the video and give it a go. I'll wait!
lines.caption: Now it's your turn. Pause the video and give it a go. I'll wait!

lines.text: Welcome back! Here's a neat trick: treat each wall like a mirror.
lines.caption: Welcome back! Here's a neat trick: treat each wall like a mirror.

lines.text: Reflect our region in the bottom wall. Now the fence has four pieces.
lines.caption: Reflect our region in the bottom wall. Now the fence has four pieces.

lines.text: Now reflect everything in the side wall too. The walls vanish inside one closed shape!
lines.caption: Now reflect everything in the side wall too. The walls vanish inside one closed shape!

lines.text: It has eight fence pieces, so it's an octagon. Its perimeter is four times twelve, forty-eight.
lines.caption: It has eight fence pieces, so it's an octagon. Its perimeter is four times twelve, forty-eight.

lines.text: Its area is four times our region. So we want the biggest octagon with perimeter forty-eight.
lines.caption: Its area is four times our region. So we want the biggest octagon with perimeter forty-eight.

lines.text: Here's a fact worth knowing. For a fixed perimeter, a circle holds the most area.
lines.caption: Here's a fact worth knowing. For a fixed perimeter, a circle holds the most area.

lines.text: With eight straight sides, the winner is the regular octagon, with equal sides and equal angles.
lines.caption: With eight straight sides, the winner is the regular octagon, with equal sides and equal angles.

lines.text: Can our fence make one? Place the center of the octagon at the corner O, and turn it to fit.
lines.caption: Can our fence make one? Place the center of the octagon at the corner O, and turn it to fit.

lines.text: Its corners are forty-five degrees apart. So the walls, ninety degrees apart, hold two sides.
lines.caption: Its corners are forty-five degrees apart. So the walls, ninety degrees apart, hold two sides.

lines.text: Each side is forty-eight over eight, which is six. Two pieces of six: that's our fence!
lines.caption: Each side is forty-eight over eight, which is six. Two pieces of six: that's our fence!

lines.text: Now the area. Turn the octagon so a side sits flat. It's a square with its corners cut off.
lines.caption: Now the area. Turn the octagon so a side sits flat. It's a square with its corners cut off.

lines.text: Each cut corner has equal legs and a long side of six.
lines.caption: Each cut corner has equal legs and a long side of six.

lines.text: In a forty-five forty-five ninety triangle, the long side is a leg times root two. So each leg is three root two.
lines.caption: In a forty-five forty-five ninety triangle, the long side is a leg times root two. So each leg is three root two.

lines.text: Along the top: a leg, then six, then another leg. That adds up to six plus six root two.
lines.caption: Along the top: a leg, then six, then another leg. That adds up to six plus six root two.

lines.text: Squared, that's one hundred eight, plus seventy-two root two.
lines.caption: Squared, that's one hundred eight, plus seventy-two root two.

lines.text: Each corner triangle has area nine. So the four corners cut away thirty-six.
lines.caption: Each corner triangle has area nine. So the four corners cut away thirty-six.

lines.text: That leaves seventy-two plus seventy-two root two for the octagon.
lines.caption: That leaves seventy-two plus seventy-two root two for the octagon.

lines.text: Our region is one quarter of it: <short pause> eighteen plus eighteen root two! That's choice B.
lines.caption: Our region is one quarter of it: eighteen plus eighteen root two! That's choice B.

lines.text: That's about forty-three and a half. Much better than thirty-six!
lines.caption: That's about forty-three and a half. Much better than thirty-six!

lines.text: Here's a second way, with just one idea: tallest in the middle.
lines.caption: Here's a second way, with just one idea: tallest in the middle.

lines.text: Join A to B. With the bend pointing out, that cuts our region into two triangles.
lines.caption: Join A to B. With the bend pointing out, that cuts our region into two triangles.

lines.text: The corner triangle has a right angle at O. So O sits on a half circle over A B.
lines.caption: The corner triangle has a right angle at O. So O sits on a half circle over A B.

lines.text: The outer triangle has A P plus P B equal to twelve, like a loop of string pinned at A and B.
lines.caption: The outer triangle has A P plus P B equal to twelve, like a loop of string pinned at A and B.

lines.text: Whatever A B is, both triangles are tallest right in the middle.
lines.caption: Whatever A B is, both triangles are tallest right in the middle.

lines.text: So in the best shape, O A equals O B, and both fence pieces are six.
lines.caption: So in the best shape, O A equals O B, and both fence pieces are six.

lines.text: Now cut along O P. We get two matching triangles, each with an angle of forty-five degrees at O.
lines.caption: Now cut along O P. We get two matching triangles, each with an angle of forty-five degrees at O.

lines.text: Stand one on its side A P. Points that see A P at forty-five degrees lie on one arc.
lines.caption: Stand one on its side A P. Points that see A P at forty-five degrees lie on one arc.

lines.text: Tallest in the middle again! So O A equals O P.
lines.caption: Tallest in the middle again! So O A equals O P.

lines.text: Now A, P and B are all the same distance from O. Each piece spans forty-five degrees.
lines.caption: Now A, P and B are all the same distance from O. Each piece spans forty-five degrees.

lines.text: Eight of those go all the way around. It's the regular octagon again! Same answer.
lines.caption: Eight of those go all the way around. It's the regular octagon again! Same answer.

lines.text: When would you pick this way? When you want to see WHY the balanced shape wins.
lines.caption: When would you pick this way? When you want to see WHY the balanced shape wins.

lines.text: Now, let's look at the wrong answers. Each one is a trap.
lines.caption: Now, let's look at the wrong answers. Each one is a trap.

lines.text: A is the six by six square. It fits, but it's not the biggest.
lines.caption: A is the six by six square. It fits, but it's not the biggest.

lines.text: E is the whole octagon. Remember, our region is just one quarter of it!
lines.caption: E is the whole octagon. Remember, our region is just one quarter of it!

lines.text: C is thirty-six root two, about fifty-one. D is thirty-six plus eighteen root two, about sixty-one.
lines.caption: C is thirty-six root two, about fifty-one. D is thirty-six plus eighteen root two, about sixty-one.

lines.text: But no region beats forty-three and a half!
lines.caption: But no region beats forty-three and a half!

lines.text: Great habit: estimate each choice, and cross out the impossible ones.
lines.caption: Great habit: estimate each choice, and cross out the impossible ones.

lines.text: Ready for a twist? Same corner, but now the fence is ONE straight piece, ten long.
lines.caption: Ready for a twist? Same corner, but now the fence is ONE straight piece, ten long.

lines.text: What's the largest area it can enclose? Use the same mirror trick!
lines.caption: What's the largest area it can enclose? Use the same mirror trick!

lines.text: Pause the video, and go for it!
lines.caption: Pause the video, and go for it!

lines.text: Let's check. Reflect in both walls. Four sides of ten. Find the biggest one with perimeter forty.
lines.caption: Let's check. Reflect in both walls. Four sides of ten. Find the biggest one with perimeter forty.

lines.text: The regular one wins again: a square with side ten, and area one hundred.
lines.caption: The regular one wins again: a square with side ten, and area one hundred.

lines.text: Our region is one quarter of it: <short pause> twenty-five!
lines.caption: Our region is one quarter of it: twenty-five!

lines.text: Check: both legs are five root two. Half of five root two, times five root two, is twenty-five.
lines.caption: Check: both legs are five root two. Half of five root two, times five root two, is twenty-five.

lines.text: If you found twenty-five, fantastic work!
lines.caption: If you found twenty-five, fantastic work!

lines.text: Here's the big idea to remember.
lines.caption: Here's the big idea to remember.

lines.text: When a fence meets straight walls, mirror it. The walls disappear, and you get a closed shape.
lines.caption: When a fence meets straight walls, mirror it. The walls disappear, and you get a closed shape.

lines.text: Same perimeter, same number of sides: the regular shape holds the most area.
lines.caption: Same perimeter, same number of sides: the regular shape holds the most area.

lines.text: I'm Vantee. Keep exploring, and I'll see you next time!
lines.caption: I'm Vantee. Keep exploring, and I'll see you next time!
